pr_title: soc: stm32: SEGGER RTT requires some extra configuration
pr_body:
soc: stm32: SEGGER RTT requires some extra configuration

On some STM32 boards, for unclear reason,
RTT feature is working with realtime update only when
  * one of the DMA is clocked
and sometimes also
  * one of the DBGMCU bit STOP/STANDBY/SLEEP is set
 
Fixes #34324
pr_comments:
I tested on STM32L443VC, it's working perfectly. 
But when I tested on STM32L073VZ, the firmware logic running ok, but the MCU seems dead while RTT Viewer connected, after disconnected the MCU reseted automatically.

Before applied the patch, on STM32L073VZ board the firmware logic will run but the MCU stop working right after RTT connected. So this may not related to this patch, just another issue caused the RTT not working on STM32L073VZ.

@ghlualven, I agree that RTT is still not working on L073.
I made a status of RTT functioning across stm32 series based on this patch:




Serie | Board | RTT status
-- | -- | --
F1 | nucleo_f103rb | OK
F2 | nucleo_f207zg | OK
F3 | nucleo_f303re | OK
F4 | nucleo_f429zi | OK
F7 | nucleo_f746zg | OK
G0 | nucleo_g071rb | OK
L4 | nucleo_l476rg | Ok
L5 | nucleo_l552re | OK
WB | nucleo_wb55rg | OK
  |   |  
L0 | nucleo_l073rz | KO
L1 | nucleo_l152re | KO
F0 | Nucleo_f091rc | KO

For other series, I could not test because I could not reflash stlink to jlink and I don't have specific mipi10 connector required on those borads to use my homemade Jlink.

Unfortunately, I could not understand why it fails on L0, L1, F0. And even worse, why MCU doesn't work properly when RTT connected for those series. I don't understand how RTT can prevent MCU to run properly. And hard to debug, as when debugger is attached then everything is working well (MCU + RTT).

My proposal is to merge this PR even there is still some non working series,
but at least, it fixes F1, L4 and F4 issues.

@erwango, the goal was to fix #10739, as debugging over the J-Link worked way better for me (*used flashed ST-LINK On-Board*).
If I remember correctly, the [SystemView ](https://www.segger.com/products/development-tools/systemview/) didn't work for me as well. However, I didn't dive into that back in the day.

I spend some time investigating this issue, and here are my findings.
My current status:
RTT is working on:
* nucleo_f429zi
* nucleo_l4r5zi
* stm32f3_disco

RTT is not working on:
* nucleo_f411re
* nucleo_l476rg

During my investigations, I figure out that even on "not working" boards (nucleo_l476rg mainly used to debug), it is possible to make it work:
* RTT is working when a debugger is attached, and I break CPU.
It means that RTTviewer did not get live update of messages while cpu is running, but a soon as I break CPU, RTTviewer get all messages (including those 'send' while running)
It means also that when debugging step by step it works fine (because CPU is implicitly stopped after each step) … which doesn't help to debug ☹
So it seems all mechanisms (Zephyr RTT port) to write data to RAM are working fine. But RTT viewer did succeed to access it while CPU is running.

* When adding RTT trace within zephyr kernel initialization (so before scheduling), RTTviewer get those traces provided that either I reduce system clock (for example default reset MSI) or I add some active waiting loop after traces (while loop).
My feeling is that in both cases we let enough time for RTTviewer to get the messages before starting zephyr scheduler.
But adding traces in 'main' function (so after scheduling is started), those traces are not shown in RTTviewer with the same conditions. So Scheduling seems to be the key point.
In other words, without zephyr scheduling RTT is working fine.

* When adding RTT trace in 'main' function (after scheduling), RTTviewer get those traces on condition that I replace k_msleep() by an active loop (either k_busy_wait() or while loop),
(no need to reduce system clock).
And if I mixes both k_msleep() and active loop, RTT may work depending on values for k_msleep and while loop.
In other words, without zephyr scheduling RTT is working fine.

Note: the state of CONFIG_MPU has no effect
  and CONFIG_PM also has no effect

I compare nucleo_l476rg and nucleo_l4r5zi  , both have the same compilation switch/kconfig enabled,
except of course dedicated switches like CONFIG_SOC, CONFIG_BOARD, CONFIG_FLASH_SIZE, CONFIG_SRAM_SIZE, CONFIG_NUM_IRQS. And that is all.
They have the same system clock.
I took the  exact nucleo_l476rg binary (not working), and I flashed it to nucleo_l4r5zi  … RTT is working fine on nucleo_l4r5zi  !!!

So it seems that there is an hardware difference between l476rg and l4r5zi, (probably similar to diff between f411re and f429zi),
which, in combination with zephyr scheduling causes RTT viewer to no accessing RAM while CPU is running. 
Any help from Zephyr scheduler experts is welcome .

A bit more investigation shows that it is not linked to zephyr scheduler, but simply to WFI instruction. 
Problem vanished when WFI is replaced (for test purpose) by a NOP.

Thank @ABOSTM for the extensive experiments. wfi -> nop leads me to think about the sleep / standby mode. 

STM32 has a debug register DBGMCU. It contains bits controlling low power behavior, c.f. [RM0008](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/cd00171190-stm32f101xx-stm32f102xx-stm32f103xx-stm32f105xx-and-stm32f107xx-advanced-arm-based-32-bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) and [AN4989](https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/dm00354244-stm32-microcontroller-debug-toolbox-stmicroelectronics.pdf).

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/90120048/132127834-6d3b268d-69de-4e37-9795-2ce851feb283.png)

I have just done some experiments on Nucleo_F103RB. Previously there was no output until the target is halted. Now there is at least some incomplete output when the target is running.

I will continue to explore it and would appreciate any suggestions.

Further found out that DMA1 EN bit should be set in RCC_AHBENR register (@ 0x4002 1014). The description is in RM0008 rev. 21 p.g. 111., although it does not mention its relationship with AHB-AP.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/90120048/132182970-0863c294-f03f-4b77-ba35-3e2a7b365e71.png)

I am only having a nucleo_f103rb in my hands at this moment. Could someone confirm this on other boards?

@jaybuckeye06 tested it on a nucleol433 and it works.
setting **DBG_SLEEP**, **DBG_STOP**, and **DBG_STANDBY** to 1 in the **DBGMCU_CR** and enabling one of the DMA channels in **RCC_AHB1ENR**  seems to do the trick

@jaybuckeye06 , @mass-anis ,
Thanks for your help, that is a good catch, enabling clock of DMA (either DMA1 or DMA2) works !!!
As far as DBGMCU bits, it is not mandatory for STM32L476, but it is mandatory for STM32F103.

So I made a PR #38561 to activate DMA clock and setting one of DBGMCU bit.
I hope it will be sufficient for all STM32 boards.

And I don't think this patch could have negative impact on RTT.
